adjudication.reason: A free developer account lets anyone build, but apps stay private to the Front instance that created them. Letting other customers connect one requires publishing it, which means Front tests it and may also run a security or legal review. That is the vendor-review gate the admin_approval definition describes.

The schema lists "app review for public use" under build_with_caveat.

adjudication.reason: Besides OAuth 2.0, Zoho Cliq lets each user generate static Webhook Tokens. These are passed as a zapikey query parameter on its api/v2 endpoints so third-party apps can post to channels and bots. That counts as a static key/token, which A missed.
adjudication.quote: Webhook Tokens are unique authentication keys designed for individual users on the Cliq platform.

adjudication.reason: A free custom app only works inside the tenant that built it. For users in other tenants to connect, you need a Store app, and Lark's docs say only accounts with ISV (service-provider) qualification can create one. That qualification is a partner application, which is a stricter gate than self_serve_free (A) or app review alone (B).

adjudication.reason: Store admins generate the consumer key and secret themselves in WP admin, with no partner program, app review or paid plan, and anyone can stand up a free self-hosted test store. None of the build_with_caveat triggers apply: the REST API is broad. A's reasons are real friction (no OAuth2, a per-store URL, an MCP still in preview) but are not caveats under these definitions.

That is the "paid plan" limit the build_with_caveat definition describes, not self-serve build_now. Once the store is upgraded, a custom app's credentials are generated automatically in the dashboard, so it falls short of needs_outreach.

adjudication.reason: Any registered user gets working credentials free, plus a free Sandbox for API testing. The $1 credit has no stated time limit, so it is free credit, not a time-limited trial. The $50 top-up is the cost of production usage, not the gate to getting credentials.
adjudication.quote: You can also test API integration for free using the DataForSEO Sandbox.

adjudication.reason: PitchBook's docs say existing clients request API access from inside the Platform (Plugins & Apps, via the Direct Data team or account manager), which fits customer_account. They also call the API a separate offering that needs its own contract, which means going through sales and fits partner_gated. Slight lean to customer_account. Caveat: no pages were opened directly; evidence comes from search-result summaries, and the URL for the quoted sentence is a best guess.
